plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in Australian cities turn hazy lavender-blue as this tree drapes itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped blossoms. The fallen flowers carpet pavements and parked cars in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late October through November, with the peak in early to mid November
plants.location: Eastern Australia, including Brisbane and Sydney
plants.funFact: Jacarandas often flower before the fern-like leaves fully return, so the tree looks like a cloud of purple. In Australia, the bloom has long been linked with university exam season.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub brightens the shortening days of autumn with delicate, often fragrant flowers. Their petals are silky and their golden stamens form a bright center.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, generally from October or November through December or January
plants.location: Southern Japan, its native range, and mild-climate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias bloom months before their showier cousin, Camellia japonica. Their leaves are close relatives of those used to make tea.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum morifolium
plants.description: Chrysanthemums unfurl dense, layered blooms in autumn gardens and flower shows, from tight pompoms to spidery, shaggy starbursts. In Japan, they are celebrated in dedicated autumn exhibitions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, roughly September to November in Japan
plants.location: Japan, including gardens such as Tokyo's Shinjuku Gyoen
plants.funFact: The chrysanthemum is Japan's imperial emblem. Because it flowers in response to lengthening nights, growers can shade the plants to bring on blooms at will.
